newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African gangsters commemorate leader's slaying.
newsitem.headline: S.African gangsters commemorate leader's slaying.

text.p: More than 1,000 Cape Town gangsters, many with barely concealed weapons, gathered on an open field on Monday to commemorate the brutal killing a year ago of their leader, Rashaad Staggie.
A crowd, estimated by some organisers on the scene at over 2,000, gathered in the gang stronghold of Manenberg to pay tribute to the former "Hard Livings" leader.
Organisers said they planned later to drive in convoy to the Salt River home where Staggie was wounded by Moslem militants and then burned alive a year ago.
The killing followed a march by the Moslem militant movement People Against Gangsterism and Drugs (Pagad) on what they said was the home of a known drug dealer.
Since then, armed Pagad demonstrators, who usually mask their faces with Palestinian-style scarves, have attacked more than 50 houses which, they allege, are used to peddle drugs.
Staggie's slow death was recorded on film and video and seen around the world, but police so far have failed to convict anyone in the crowd of Pagad activists.
Police, who have warned that tension between Pagad and the gangs is building to a critical point, stood by on Monday, but did not attempt to halt the gathering.
Many of the gangsters and their followers who attended Monday's commemoration carried what appeared to be rifles or shotguns in leather cases or wrapped in blankets.
The ceremony was attended by Staggie's twin brother, Rashied, who now leads the feared "Hard Livings" gang, one of scores that control life in Cape Town's working-class areas.
Pagad members anticipated Monday's commemoration with a gathering of their own on Sunday.
About 2,000 members of the vigilante group, many of them masked and several apparently armed, staged a two-hour march through some of Cape Town's poorest areas.
Speakers reaffirmed their vow to halt the trade in drugs and break the dominance of the gangs in the mainly mixed-race or coloured suburbs.
